facts.text: The rooftop chase was shot over eleven nights on a single soundstage, with the city skyline built as a forty foot model.
Mara Quill learned to ride a motorcycle for the role and did most of the courier scenes herself.
Every neon sign in the film was designed to be unreadable, so the city would feel like no real place.
The score was recorded on a modular synthesizer that the composer kept running for the full eight weeks of the shoot.
Dorian Vale auditioned for the courier before being offered the role of the memory broker.
The rain was warmed to body temperature so the cast could stay in it for long takes.
In the train station scene, the courier's coat changes from left to right buttoning between shots.
The song playing in the noodle bar was written in an afternoon and later became the main theme.
The memory erasing device was built from a vintage camera lens and a car headlight.
Imani Brooks shot all of her scenes in nine days while filming another project.
A crew member's reflection is visible in a puddle during the final rooftop scene.
The film's city has its own map, drawn before the script was finished.
